page: Vultr voc-c-32c-64gb-500s-amd is an instance in the Optimized Cloud Compute family, configured with a compute-focused resource allocation. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features a dedicated 2.0 GHz AMD EPYC processor delivering 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU cache architecture comprises 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. It incorporates vector instruction extensions including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 support, alongside hardware-accelerated cryptographic instructions like AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

System memory consists of 64.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio with 2.0 GB allocated per thread. The server includes 500 GB of attached local NVMe SSD storage and one public IPv4 address, without integrated GPU hardware accelerators. Benchmark evaluations reveal top-tier single-core stress-ng processing and strong multi-core execution across stress-ng, Geekbench 6, PassMark CPU tests, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. The system also registers strong performance in Clang software compilation and CPU encryption workloads, while memory bandwidth and static web throughput operate in the middle tier.

This server provides balanced cost efficiency for high-density compute tasks requiring dedicated CPU cores without the premium overhead of GPU acceleration or large memory footprints. The 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio makes it less suitable for memory-intensive in-memory databases, but it represents a capable profile for parallelized software compilation, continuous integration pipelines, batch data processing, CPU-based machine learning inference, and high-concurrency microservices.
description: Vultr voc-c-32c-64gb-500s-amd is a compute-focused virtual machine within the Optimized Cloud Compute family. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs spanning 16 physical cores on an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, complemented by 64.0 GB of memory and 500 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The CPU supports AVX-512 extensions including VNNI and BF16, as well as hardware cryptographic acceleration. Performance benchmarks demonstrate top-tier single-core compute performance and strong multi-core scalability across Geekbench, PassMark, and software compilation tasks. With a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio and dedicated CPU allocation, this configuration operates effectively for parallel build pipelines, batch data processing, CPU inference, and web serving architectures.
